environment: Mon Repos rangers gear up as the first loggerhead turtles are spotted scouting Queensland beaches for spring nesting season
A new grid-scale battery in regional Queensland flicks the switch, banking sunshine for the state's growing renewable stockpile
science: Queensland marine scientists notch up another win in the coral IVF program, giving battered reef patches a spring growth spurt
sports: Junior rugby league sign-ups across Queensland surge as spring comp season kicks off in the school holidays
stories.overview: Brisbane 2032 organisers unveil plans for a sun powered Olympic Village that could make the Games the greenest on record

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: Morning legends, it is Wednesday the thirtieth of September and you are locked in with ParkSyde Bright Side. I am Alex Mercer, feeling pretty chipper because spring has well and truly kicked the doona off Queensland. Big show today, reef babies, battery power and a bit of Olympic dreaming. And I am Jamie, buzzing because it is officially turtle watch season down at Mon Repos. Honestly nothing says good news bulletin like an ancient reptile waddling up a beach at midnight. We have got the environment, science, sport and Sam with the weather all lined up for you. Straight into it then, because this bulletin waits for no one, not even a turtle. Let us start where we always start, with some genuinely good news for the planet.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: First up, rangers at Mon Repos near Bundaberg reckon they have already clocked early scouting loggerheads cruising the shallows, checking out real estate for nesting season. It is one of the biggest turtle rookeries on the east coast of Australia and every spring it kicks off like clockwork. Love that, nature's real estate agents doing their rounds before the rest of us have even had our coffee. Meanwhile out west a brand new grid scale battery has just started pumping stored sunshine back into the grid, which is a solid boost for keeping the lights on when the sun clocks off. Big batteries, bigger turtles, and both of them quietly making Queensland a bit more sustainable. That is the green wrap, short, sweet and full of good vibes.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Onto science now, and our reef scientists just will not stop tinkering. The coral IVF crews have had another promising spawn of lab grown coral babies ready to be seeded back onto damaged patches of the Great Barrier Reef. Coral IVF still sounds like something out of a sci-fi movie to me, but it is very real and very clever. Basically they collect coral spawn, grow it up safe and sound, then give the reef a helping hand exactly where it needs it most. It is slow, patient work but it is paying off in patches of reef that are genuinely bouncing back. Good on them, because someone has got to look after the world's biggest living structure.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and good morning everyone, Sam here with your south east Queensland outlook. Spring is doing exactly what it should, Brisbane is looking at a cracker day with clear skies and a top around twenty six degrees, while the Gold and Sunshine Coasts will see a gentle sea breeze roll in through the afternoon to keep things comfortable. Inland spots like Ipswich and Toowoomba will run a touch warmer, so pack the sunnies, keep the water bottle handy, and enjoy one of those postcard spring days we do so well up here.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sportswise, it is school holidays which means it is also junior footy sign up season, and the numbers coming through for girls rugby league this year are seriously impressive. Clubs right across Queensland are reporting waiting lists, which is the kind of problem every coach wants to have. I love that, a whole new generation growing up thinking footy for girls is just completely normal. Give it a few years and we will be watching some of these kids running out in Maroon on the big stage. That is the dream alright. Grassroots sport doing exactly what it is meant to do, getting kids outside and having a crack.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Now for today's big feel good moment, and it is a ripper. Organisers behind the twenty thirty two Brisbane Olympics have unveiled early plans for an Olympic Village that runs almost entirely on solar power. An Olympic Village powered by sunshine, in Queensland, be still my heart. If any state was built for that job it is us, we have got sunshine to burn. Exactly, and it would set a genuine benchmark for how future Games get built and powered. Athletes from around the world sleeping under Queensland sunshine, quite literally. That is a lovely note to finish on. Turtles scouting beaches, batteries humming, reef babies growing and an Olympic Village dreaming big, honestly what a Wednesday. That is ParkSyde Bright Side done and dusted for today. I am Alex, that is Jamie, catch you tomorrow for more good news, stay sunny Queensland.
